title: Cap. IV Arg. 3 Sol close: Minor true of medium — not eligere credentes; Rom. 9:15
pass_a_gloss: Now I come to the Minor, which consists in those words of the Apostle, To will to save believers by the foolishness of preaching is God's good pleasure concerning human salvation. Who denies it? For it is God's good pleasure concerning the means and organ, without whose help no one of adult age can be led to salvation. But it does not express that eternal good pleasure of εὐδοκία according to which certain ones are elected to salvation and the means of salvation, others being passed by. In a word; the Apostle said, It pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save believers. He therefore requires preaching, and faith, as means antecedent from God's good pleasure to effecting salvation itself. He did not say, It pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to elect believers. He therefore does not require faith, or preaching, as conditions foreseen and antecedent to the eternal act of election. Nor do those things avail hither which were brought concerning unbelievers from 1 Cor. 10 and from Heb. 3. For those places do not prove that God from eternity elects, or passes by men from antecedent foresight of faith or unbelief future in them; but that God in the execution of his eternal decree finally introduces into his rest those whom by efficacious vocation, and working according to purpose, he has rendered faithful; but excludes those who by the corrupt perversity of their own heart remain unbelieving. But why he will have had mercy on these rather than those, do not seek, if you do not will to err. Let that suffice, I will have mercy on whom I will have had mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have had compassion, Rom. 9:15.
pass_b_english: Now the Minor: to will to save believers by the foolishness of preaching is God's good pleasure concerning human salvation. Who denies it? It is good pleasure about the means and organ without which no adult can be led to salvation. It does not express that eternal εὐδοκία by which some are elected to salvation and its means, others passed by. In a word: the Apostle said It pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save believers — so he requires preaching and faith as means antecedent by God's good pleasure to effecting salvation. He did not say to elect believers. So he does not require faith or preaching as foreseen antecedent conditions of the eternal act of election. Nor do 1 Cor. 10 and Heb. 3 on unbelievers help: they do not prove eternal election or passing-by from foresight of future faith or unbelief, but that in executing his eternal decree God finally brings into his rest those whom efficacious vocation working according to purpose has made faithful, and excludes those who remain unbelieving by their own heart's corrupt perversity. Why he had mercy on these rather than those — do not ask, if you would not err. Suffice Rom. 9:15: I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy.
source_text: Jam accedo ad Minorem, quae illis Apostoli verbis constat, Credentes velle salvare per stultitiam praedicationis est beneplacitum Dei de salute humana. Quis negat? Est enim beneplacitum Dei de medio et organo, absque quorum ope ad salutem nemo adulta aetate perduci potest. Sed non exprimit illud aeternum εὐδοκίας beneplacitum secundum quod quidam ad salutem et salutis media, praeteritis aliis, eliguntur. Uno verbo; dixit Apostolus, Placuit Deo per stultitiam praedicationis servare credentes. Requirit igitur praedicationem, et fidem, tanquam media ex Dei beneplacito ad ipsam salutem efficiendam antecedanea. Non dixit, Placuit Deo per stultitiam praedicationis eligere credentes. Non igitur requirit fidem, aut praedicationem, tanquam conditiones praevisas et antecedaneas ad aeternum actum electionis. Neque huc faciunt quae de incredulis ex 1 Cor. x. et ex Hebr. iii. allata fuerunt. Ea enim loca non probant Deum ab aeterno eligere, aut praeterire homines ex antecedanea praevisione fidei aut incredulitatis in iis futurae; sed Deum in exsecutione aeterni sui decreti, tandem introducere eos in requiem suam, quos vocatione efficaci, et secundum propositum operante, reddidit fideles; eos autem excludere, qui proprii cordis corrupta perversitate manent increduli. Cur autem horum potius quam illorum misertus fuerit, noli quaerere, si non vis errare. Sufficiat illud, Miserebor cujus misertus fuero, et commiserabor quem commiseratus fuero, Rom. ix. 15.
